bib.title: Optuna: A Next-generation Hyperparameter Optimization Framework

question: What design criteria should a next-generation hyperparameter optimization framework meet, and does Optuna meet them?
hypothesis: A define-by-run API, combined efficient sampling and pruning, and an easy-to-set-up scalable architecture together give cost-effective optimization.
contributions: Define-by-run API that builds the search space dynamically
Efficient implementation of sampling and pruning (ASHA variant; TPE+CMA-ES mixture)
Easy-to-setup, versatile architecture from notebook to distributed (shared storage)

method.summary: Optuna is an open-source (MIT) HPO framework where the objective function receives a trial object and calls suggest_* to build the search space at runtime. It supports independent (TPE) and relational (CMA-ES, GP-BO) sampling, an Asynchronous Successive Halving pruner, and a shared-storage design (in-memory, SQLite or RDB) for distributed runs.

datasets.name: Black-box optimization test collection (evalset / Dewancker et al.)

inference.samples: Sec 5.1: each study repeated 30 times per algorithm, 80 trials per study. Sec 5.2: each study repeated 40 times, 4 hours each.

parameters.TPE+CMA-ES: TPE for the first 40 steps, CMA-ES for the rest (Sec 5.1)
parameters.Successive Halving pruner inputs: minimum resource r, reduction factor eta, minimum early-stopping rate s (values not stated)
parameters.Pruning rule: trial promoted if provisional rank within top 1/eta at its rung; no repechage

other.hardware_pruning_exp: one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study
other.RocksDB: 34 of 100+ parameters tuned; default 372 s on HDD, tuned 30 s; 4 h budget

metrics.name: best attained objective value in 80 trials
metrics.definition: best value found per study, compared by paired Mann-Whitney U test

metrics.name: average test error
metrics.definition: test error of simplified AlexNet on SVHN over time

metrics.name: trials per study
metrics.definition: number of trials completed or explored within 4 hours

eval.protocol: Paired Mann-Whitney U test, alpha = 0.0005, 30 repeats (Sec 5.1); 40 repeats (Sec 5.2).

results.claim: Without pruning, TPE completes about 36 trials per study in 4 hours.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; TPE without pruning
results.quote: On average, TPE and random search without pruning completed 35.8 and 36.0 trials per study, respectively.

results.claim: Without pruning, random search completes about 36 trials per study in 4 hours.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; random search without pruning
results.quote: On average, TPE and random search without pruning completed 35.8 and 36.0 trials per study, respectively.

results.claim: With ASHA pruning, TPE explores about 1279 trials per study in 4 hours.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; TPE with pruning
results.quote: TPE with pruning explored 1278.6 trials on average per study, of which 1271.5 were pruned during the process.

results.claim: Of the TPE+pruning trials, 1271.5 on average were pruned.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; TPE with pruning
results.quote: TPE with pruning explored 1278.6 trials on average per study, of which 1271.5 were pruned during the process.

results.claim: With pruning, random search explores about 1119 trials per study in 4 hours.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; random search with pruning
results.quote: Random search with pruning explored 1119.3 trials with 1111.3 pruned trials.

results.claim: Of the random search+pruning trials, 1111.3 on average were pruned.
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting; random search with pruning
results.quote: Random search with pruning explored 1119.3 trials with 1111.3 pruned trials.

results.claim: ASHA pruning beats median pruning and accelerates both TPE and random search (read from Fig 11a; no number in text).
results.setup: Simplified AlexNet (3 conv layers + 1 FC, 8 hyperparameters) on SVHN, one NVIDIA Tesla P100 per study, 4 hours per study, 40 repeats per setting
results.quote: Our implementation of ASHA signiﬁcantly outperforms Median pruning, a pruning method featured in Vizier.

results.claim: TPE+CMA-ES is statistically worse than random search in only 1/56 test cases.
results.setup: 56 black-box test cases, 80 trials, 30 repeats, paired Mann-Whitney U alpha=0.0005
results.quote: TPE+CMA-ES ﬁnds statistically worse solution than random search in only 1/56 test cases

results.claim: GPyOpt beat TPE+CMA-ES in 34/56 cases but needed about twenty times longer per study.
results.quote: GPyOpt performed better than TPE+CMA-ES in 34/56 cases in terms of the best-attained loss value.

results.claim: RocksDB tuning with pruning cut run time from 372 s to 30 s; 937 parameter sets explored with pruning vs 39 without in 4 hours.
results.setup: RocksDB, 500,000 files of 10KB, 34 parameters, HDD, 4 h
results.quote: With pruning, Optuna was able to ﬁnd a parameter-set that reduces the computation time to 30 seconds.

results.claim: Without a time-out and without pruning, only 2 RocksDB trials complete in 4 hours.
results.setup: RocksDB, no evaluation time-out, no pruning
results.quote: When we disable the time-out option for the evaluation process, the algorithm without pruning explores only 2 trials.

results.claim: Distributed optimization scales linearly with workers; score per trial barely changes with 1, 2, 4, 8 workers.
results.setup: TPE, 1/2/4/8 workers, same setup as Sec 5.2
results.quote: This shows that the performance is linearly scaling with the number of trials, and hence with the number of workers.

limits: Experiments report no confidence intervals in text; pruning results are figures (Fig 11) with only trial counts in text.
Pruner hyperparameters (r, eta, s) for the experiments are not stated.
Pruning experiment uses one simplified AlexNet/SVHN task; the trial-count gain (about 35x) mixes more trials explored with more trials pruned early.
Time-out used for no-pruning RocksDB baseline is not specified.
2019 preprint; Optuna's API has since changed (e.g. suggest_loguniform, optuna.Study(name, storage)) and later versions are not covered.

terms.definition: a design that allows the user to dynamically construct the search space
Optuna refers to each process of optimization as a study, and to each evaluation of objective function as a trial
termination of unpromising trials based on intermediate values; automated early stopping, named differently from early-stopping regularization
